nws.synopsis: A subtle cooling trend with cloudier skies and a rainier outlook is on tap as we head toward the weekend. The heaviest rainfall is expected later on Saturday into Sunday. Slightly warmer temperatures and dry weather is expected by Monday into the middle of next week.
systems: A weak troughing pattern will continue across the region today into Thursday.
The marine layer will begin to build further in the days ahead with better chances for low clouds to fill parts of the coastal basin each night and morning.
A low pressure system currently over British Columbia will move southward Thursday into Friday, near the coasts of Washington and Oregon.
As it does so, the troughing pattern will become stronger, bringing in slightly cooler weather and a deeper marine layer.

nws.aviation: 290230Z...SCT-BKN marine layer clouds based 2500-3000 ft MSL are currently filling in for coasts and valleys up to 20 miles inland. A lower layer may develop near 2000 ft MSL sometime 04-08z Thu. Coverage of low clouds should become more uniform near the coast overnight, but remain intermittent for inland valleys with occasional scattering. Low clouds push into the Inland Empire after 06z, but coverage in this zone should remain patchy. Low clouds scatter back to the coast 15-18z, though SCT low clouds may hang over coastal areas all day, especially in San Diego County. Low clouds based 2500-3500 ft MSL rush back inland early Thursday evening.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. Launch in the light air before the switch; the west wind then builds the convergence inland (Perris, Hemet, Soboba). XC wants 7-8k over the range during the switch and the same or more inland.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse
sites.note: Two launches: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert. Each is scored on its own and the better one is shown.

sites.name: Santa Barbara (Skyport)
sites.note: South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back.

sites.name: Owens Valley (Walt's Point)
sites.note: Watch only: shows when it rates 5. Advanced pilots only. Morning site with very strong thermals, cloudbase 13-20k. Needs light winds; west wind over the Sierra is a no-go. PGs don't fly it June to early September.
